t.1.191.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Now that Drupada had entered into alliance with the Pāṇḍavas, he had no fear whatsoever from anyone, not even from the gods.
t.1.191.2: Having approached Kuntī, those women of the great-souled Drupada, proclaiming their names, touched her feet with their own heads.
t.1.191.3: And Kṛṣṇā, clad in linen, the auspicious wedding rites having been performed for her, made her salutation to her mother-in-law and stood bowed low with joined palms.
t.1.191.4: Pṛthā lovingly spoke words of blessing to Draupadī, her daughter-in-law, who was endowed with beauty and auspicious marks and possessed of good character and conduct.
t.1.191.6: As Bhadrā is to Vaiśravaṇa, as Arundhatī is to Vasiṣṭha, and as Lakṣmī is to Nārāyaṇa, so may you be to your husbands.
t.1.191.5: As Indrāṇī is devoted to Harihaya and Svāhā to Vibhāvasu, as Rohiṇī is to Soma and as Damayantī is to Nala,
t.1.191.7: O fortunate one, may you be the mother of living sons and the mother of heroes, endowed with much happiness, beloved, rich in pleasures, a wife at the sacrifice, and truly devoted to your husbands.
t.1.191.8: May your years pass forever as you honour, in due measure, guests who have arrived, the virtuous, children, the aged, and your elders.
t.1.191.9: In the kingdoms and cities with Kurujāṅgala foremost among them, may you be consecrated along with the king who cherishes dharma.
t.1.191.11: O virtuous one, whatever excellent jewels there are on the earth, may you obtain them, O auspicious lady, and live happily for a hundred autumns.
t.1.191.10: Make over to the brahmins the whole wide earth, conquered through valor by your mighty husbands, at the great sacrifice of the horse sacrifice.
t.1.191.13: Then Hari sent to the Pāṇḍavas, who had taken a wife, golden ornaments set with pearls and beryl.
t.1.191.12: Just as I greet you today, daughter-in-law, clad in linen, so shall I greet you again when you have borne a son, you who are endowed with virtues.
t.1.191.14: Mādhava also gave costly garments from many lands, and beautiful blankets, skins and jewels, soft to the touch.
t.1.191.16: Kṛṣṇa also bestowed thousands of serving-maidens from many lands, endowed with beauty, youth and courtesy, and finely adorned.
t.1.191.15: Beds, seats and carriages of many kinds, and large ones too, and vessels by the hundreds, studded with beryl and diamonds.
t.1.191.17: Elephants, well trained and of fine breed, excellent horses richly adorned, and chariots with tamed teams, decorated with beautiful golden bands.
t.1.191.19: Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of dharma, filled with supreme joy, accepted all of that out of a desire to please Govinda.
t.1.191.18: And Madhusūdana, of immeasurable soul, sent them gold by the crore, both unwrought and wrought.
